newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on late local selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on late local selling.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on a late bout of local selling tied to day-trade profit taking, traders said.
"Locals were long and sold out. It was profit taking, longs took profits," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
"There was nothing at all that changed fundamentally. Locals just got long then got out," a trader said.
Soybeans were strong in early dealings on a surge in wheat futures with fund buying behind that rally, traders said.
Traders said slow farmer selling, active exports and mostly firm cash basis markets also were supportive.
A second consecutive day of gains in soymeal also contributed to the gains in early dealings.
The short covering in soymeal was centered in the December as that month nears expiration at 1201 CST Thursday.
Gains in soy were limited by South American weather. The South American soybean crop has benefitted from near ideal weather patterns.
Soybeans closed 1/2 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with January down 2-1/2 at $7.04.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 56,000 contracts, above the 45,351 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

Refco Inc sold 500 March $7.00 puts at 14-1/2 to 15-1/2 cents, ADM Investor Services bought 650 January $7.00 puts at 1/2 to 5/8 cent and Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 500 January $7.25 calls at 1-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, above the 12,823 traded Tuesday.
